labeling.executed_by_candidate: Run in the experiment's admitted isolated python_execute sandbox (fresh empty filesystem, no network, systemd/bubblewrap isolation). Each entry records execution_id, code_sha256, expected behavior with justification, observed stdout/exit, and scope limits.

witnesses.name: preview-sampling-is-not-proof
witnesses.input: Tiny synthetic dataset: 1000 rows, category 'A' x999 plus exactly one 'B' row; seeded (411) 20-row sample drawn twice.
witnesses.expected: A 20-row random sample misses the lone 'B' row with probability C(999,20)/C(1000,20) = 980/1000 = 0.98, while a full scan always finds it; identical seed reproduces the identical sample. Justification: combinatorial probability of excluding one specific row from a fixed-size sample without replacement.

observed.stdout_summary: sample_counts={A:20}; sample_misses_rare_category_B=true; repeat_preview_with_same_seed_identical=true; truncated marker 'showing 20 of 1000 rows'; full counts {A:999, B:1}.

witnesses.scope_limits: Pure-stdlib component check on 1000 synthetic rows; does not measure DuckDB USING SAMPLE behavior or any real reader; establishes only the epistemic point and a repeatable-seed pattern.

witnesses.name: data-contract-quarantine
witnesses.input: 7 synthetic NDJSON lines covering: valid row with Z-suffixed timestamp, null optional field, Unicode string ('naïve ✓'), wrong type in required field, missing required field, non-JSON line, impossible calendar date (month 13). Declared schema {id:int64 required, v:utf8 optional, ts:timestamp optional}, coercion policy 'quarantine'.
witnesses.expected: Rows that fail parse/type/required checks are quarantined with (offset, reason, preserved raw line); valid rows including Unicode and nulls are accepted with the timestamp normalized to ISO-8601; the original line array is never mutated.

observed.stdout_summary: accepted_count=3 (unicode_preserved=true, nulls allowed); quarantined_count=4 with per-row reasons (coercion failure, missing required field, JSONDecodeError, month must be in 1..12) and preserved raw lines; original_source_untouched=true.

witnesses.scope_limits: Component check of the contract algorithm only; does not exercise DuckDB store_rejects, Parquet, or file IO.

witnesses.name: output-status-machine + manifest round-trip
witnesses.input: Two-cell dependency chain (a -> b); deps = {dataset hash, env fingerprint, upstream cell text hash}; scenario: baseline run, edit upstream cell, mutate source dataset hash, kernel restart, re-run with failure; plus sha256 manifest serialize/reload check.
witnesses.expected: current -> downstream-only stale after upstream edit; all stale after dataset mutation; both unverified after kernel restart (session identity lost, outputs kept); failed with captured error text after a failing re-run; manifest hashes survive a JSON round-trip.

observed.stdout_summary: timeline: {a:current,b:current} -> {a:current,b:stale(cell:a)} -> {a:stale,b:stale} -> {a:unverified,b:unverified} -> {a:failed,b:unverified}; failed_error_captured='ValueError: column 'day' not found'; manifest_hash_roundtrip_ok=true.

witnesses.scope_limits: Component check of the status computation on synthetic hashes; does not prove a live kernel, real file watching, or DuckDB behavior.

witnesses.name: stable-vs-deterministic-ordering
witnesses.input: Three synthetic rows with tied sort keys, presented in two different physical orders.
witnesses.expected: Sorting by key only yields order that depends on physical input order (Python sorted is stable, so ties keep input order); adding an explicit rid tie-break yields identical order across both inputs.

observed.stdout_summary: key_only order [1,3,2] vs [3,1,2] across inputs (differs=true); (key, rid) order [1,3,2] identical across inputs.

witnesses.scope_limits: Component check in stdlib Python; database GROUP BY ordering behavior is covered by DuckDB docs facts, not by this check.

proposed_unexecuted.name: 5 GB CSV through bounded path on 16 GB machine
proposed_unexecuted.plan: Generate ~5 GB CSV; run DuckDB 1.x aggregation with SET memory_limit='9GB', SET threads=4, SET preserve_insertion_order=false, temp_directory on local SSD; record peak RSS and wall time; acceptance: completes without OOM and writes row count correct to within quarantine accounting.
proposed_unexecuted.risk_notes: DuckDB docs state some operations circumvent the buffer manager's memory limit [S10], so peak RSS may exceed memory_limit; the test must measure actual RSS, and the target is investigation, not a verified result.

proposed_unexecuted.name: crash-recovery of project saves
proposed_unexecuted.plan: Kill -9 the app during (a) event-log commit and (b) notebook JSON save; reopen; assert WAL replay restores last committed event and notebook file is either the old or new complete copy (temp+rename), never truncated; assert outputs are marked unverified if a run was in flight.

proposed_unexecuted.name: two-machine bundle open
proposed_unexecuted.plan: Zip project excluding external datasets; copy to second directory standing in for another machine; open; assert manifest hashes verify, all outputs load as unverified, and data absence is reported as unresolved source rather than silent failure.

proposed_unexecuted.name: single-writer project locking
proposed_unexecuted.plan: Open the same project from two app processes; assert the second gets an explicit advisory-lock (flock) refusal message and can open read-only; verify DuckDB file-lock error surfaces as actionable feedback consistent with DuckDB's documented concurrency model [S08].

proposed_unexecuted.name: sandbox policy conformance
proposed_unexecuted.plan: In the OS sandbox: cell attempting socket connect is blocked and the denial recorded as a run event; cell writing outside the allowlist fails with EPERM; pip install fails; resource limit (RLIMIT_AS / cpu) triggers on an infinite allocator. Acceptance: denials are visible in the UI feed, not silent.
proposed_unexecuted.risk_notes: Sandbox behavioral differences across Linux/macOS (bubblewrap vs seatbelt) may change denial modes; portability is part of the test.
